ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there are two towels, black and white, placed on the ground alternately folded; the middle of the white towel is connected to the wall with a thin string, and the middle of the black towel is pulled with a thin string. Suppose the thin strings are all horizontal. To separate the black and white towels, if the mass of each towel is m, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the towels and between them and the ground is μ, then the value of the horizontal pulling force F that needs to be applied to pull out the black towel at uniform speed is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a wall, and at the bottom is the ground; two towels are placed on the ground alternately folded, with the white towel drawn as blank layers and the black towel drawn as black layers. The middle of the white towel is connected to the left wall with a horizontal thin string, and the middle of the black towel is pulled to the right with a horizontal thin string; the pulling force F is marked on the right side. According to the stacking relationship in the figure, from top to bottom it can be regarded as four layers: upper white layer, upper black layer, lower white layer, lower black layer, with the lowest black layer in contact with the ground. Reasoning: The mass of each towel is m, and after being folded into two layers, the mass of each layer is m/2. The thin strings are all horizontal, so they do not change the normal force of each contact surface. List the sliding contact surfaces from top to bottom: 1. Between the upper white layer and the upper black layer, the upper side only bears the weight of the upper white layer, the normal force N1=(m/2)g, and the friction force f1=μN1=μmg/2; 2. Between the upper black layer and the lower white layer, above there are the upper white layer and the upper black layer, with total mass m, the normal force N2=mg, and the friction force f2=μmg; 3. Between the lower white layer and the lower black layer, above there are three layers: upper white, upper black, and lower white, with total mass 3m/2, the normal force N3=(3m/2)g, and the friction force f3=3μmg/2; 4. Between the lower black layer and the ground, the ground bears the total mass of four layers, 2m, the normal force N4=2mg, and the friction force f4=2μmg. To pull out the black towel at uniform speed, the forces on the black towel are balanced, and the horizontal pulling force F should balance the sum of these sliding friction forces: F=f1+f2+f3+f4=μmg(1/2+1+3/2+2)=5μmg.
